summary: Shows tagging a file with chtag through ansible.builtin.command. The z/OS shell assumes untagged streams are EBCDIC while Ansible sends untagged UTF-8, which is fixed by setting PYTHONSTDINENCODING so Python tags its pipe.
questions: How do I tag a file as text with chtag in Ansible?
Why does the z/OS shell misread data Ansible sends?
What does PYTHONSTDINENCODING do on z/OS?
Do all z/OS programs honour file and pipe tags?

answer_card.title: Fixing encoding mismatches with the z/OS shell
answer_card.answer_md:
Tag a file with a command task:

```yaml
- name: Tag my_file.txt as UTF-8.
  ansible.builtin.command: chtag -tc iso8859-1 my_file.txt
```

The z/OS shell treats untagged streams as EBCDIC, but Ansible sends untagged UTF-8. Set the `PYTHONSTDINENCODING` environment variable so the pipe Python uses is tagged with the right encoding. Tags allow automatic ASCII/EBCDIC conversion, but only tag-aware programs on z/OS UNIX use them.
